evidence_quote: Seven baselines are named and all are trained: "we compared its performance on two benchmark datasets with seven state-of-the-art baseline models: MNGACDA [48], GATECDA [49], MINIMDA [50], HFHLMDA [51], CGHCN [52], MIDTI [53] and DTI-CNN [41]." But the Results then add an eighth: "In addition to the aforementioned seven methods, we also compared our results with those obtained using the Heterogeneous Network that employs the Forward Similarity Integration (FSI) algorithm [42] on this dataset. We conducted five-fold cross-validation experiments and the results are presented in Table 3". Ref [42] is Tangmanussukum et al., "Heterogeneous network propagation with forward similarity integration to enhance drug-target association prediction" (PeerJ Comput Sci 2022, PMC9575853) -- an untrained propagation method that greedily selects among 7 drug and 9 target similarity measures and propagates, fitting nothing; the codebook D4 qualifying list names FSI explicitly. However Table 3 contains no FSI row (only CGHCN, GATECDA, HFHLMDA, MINIMDA, MNGACDA, MIDTI, Our model), and Fig. 3 is the training curves, so the untrained comparator is claimed in prose but its number is nowhere on the page. No verbatim quote can support "every comparator is trained" (FSI is named as compared) and none can support a table/figure appearance, so the call is unclear by the codebook cardinal rule.
